modules.title: Indexes and Query Plans
modules.goal: Choose indexes from real query shapes and read plans before adding more.

topics.title: What Is an Index?
topics.simple: Index lookup ko fast karta hai, writes ko mehnga.
topics.pro: An index is an auxiliary structure that speeds selected reads at the cost of storage and write maintenance.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_marks ON students (marks);

topics.title: B-tree Index
topics.simple: B-tree default index hai equality aur range ke liye.
topics.pro: A B-tree supports equality, ordering and range predicates and is the default PostgreSQL index type.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_marks ON students (marks DESC);

topics.title: CREATE INDEX
topics.simple: CREATE INDEX se index banao.
topics.pro: CREATE INDEX name ON table (columns) builds an index for the chosen key.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_student ON enrollments (student_id);

topics.title: Unique Index
topics.simple: Unique index duplicate values rokta hai.
topics.pro: A unique index enforces uniqueness and also speeds equality lookups.
points: It can back a primary key.

example.sql: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_students_email ON students (email);

topics.title: Composite Index
topics.simple: Composite index multiple columns ko ek order me index karta hai.
topics.pro: A composite index keys on several columns and supports predicates that use a left-hand prefix of that key.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_student_course ON enrollments (student_id, course_id);

topics.title: Index Column Order
topics.simple: Composite index ka column order usability decide karta hai.
topics.pro: The first column is the primary navigation key; putting a low-selectivity column first weakens common filters on later columns.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_course_student ON enrollments (course_id, student_id);

topics.title: Covering Index
topics.simple: INCLUDE columns se index-only scan possible hota hai.
topics.pro: INCLUDE adds payload columns to a B-tree so a query can be answered from the index without visiting the heap.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_marks_name ON students (marks) INCLUDE (name);

topics.title: Partial Index
topics.simple: Partial index sirf matching rows ko index karta hai.
topics.pro: A partial index has a WHERE predicate, so it is smaller and cheaper when only a subset is queried.
points: The query predicate must imply it.
It is ideal for rare statuses.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_known_marks ON students (marks) WHERE marks IS NOT NULL;

topics.title: Expression Index
topics.simple: Expression index function ke result ko index karta hai.
topics.pro: An expression index stores a computed key such as LOWER(name), matching queries that use the same expression.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_lower_name ON students (LOWER(name));

topics.title: Hash Index
topics.simple: Hash index equality ke liye hota hai, range ke liye nahi.
topics.pro: A hash index supports equality comparisons only and is rarely preferable to B-tree in PostgreSQL.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_email_hash ON students USING hash (email);

topics.title: GIN Index
topics.simple: GIN composite values jaise arrays aur JSONB ke liye hai.
topics.pro: GIN indexes inverted lists and is used for arrays, JSONB and full-text search.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_students_email_gin ON students USING gin (to_tsvector('simple', email));

topics.title: GiST Index
topics.simple: GiST geometric aur range data ke liye hai.
topics.pro: GiST supports extensible tree searches for geometric, range and nearest-neighbor queries.

example.sql: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_date_gist ON enrollments USING gist (enrolled_on);

topics.title: Index Selectivity
topics.simple: High selectivity wale predicates index ke liye best hain.
topics.pro: Selectivity measures how many rows a predicate removes; an index helps most when the query returns a small fraction of the table.

example.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT course_id)::numeric / COUNT(*) AS selectivity FROM enrollments;

topics.title: EXPLAIN
topics.simple: EXPLAIN plan dikhata hai bina query chalaye.
topics.pro: EXPLAIN shows the planner’s chosen access paths, join order and estimated costs without executing the statement.
points: It does not run the query.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
example.output: An Index Scan or Seq Scan plan.

topics.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
topics.simple: EXPLAIN ANALYZE query chala kar actual timing deta hai.
topics.pro: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and reports actual rows, loops and timing alongside estimates.

example.sql: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks > 90;

topics.title: Seq Scan vs Index Scan
topics.simple: Seq scan poora table padhta hai; index scan selected rows.
topics.pro: A sequential scan reads the heap linearly, while an index scan follows the index and fetches matching heap rows.
points: Seq scan is fine for large fractions.
Index scan wins for selective filters.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = 1;
example.output: An Index Scan for the primary key.

topics.title: Bitmap Scan
topics.simple: Bitmap scan index matches ko batch me heap se laata hai.
topics.pro: A bitmap heap scan builds a bitmap from one or more indexes and visits heap pages in physical order.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks BETWEEN 60 AND 70;

topics.title: Index Maintenance
topics.simple: Indexes bloat hote hain aur rebuild karne pad sakte hain.
topics.pro: Updates create index bloat; REINDEX rebuilds an index, and VACUUM helps the planner and heap health.

example.sql: REINDEX INDEX idx_students_marks;

topics.title: Common Index Mistakes
topics.simple: Unused, duplicate aur wrong-order indexes common mistakes hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are indexing low-selectivity columns, duplicating an existing prefix, and expecting an index to help every query.

example.sql: SELECT indexrelid::regclass, idx_scan FROM pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE idx_scan = 0;

topics.title: Practical Tuning
topics.simple: Query, plan, index, measure — phir repeat.
topics.pro: Tuning starts from a slow query and its plan, adds the smallest useful index, and re-measures rather than guessing.

example.sql: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 10;
example.output: A plan with buffer and timing detail.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain What Is an Index? in a production query.
interview.answer: An index is an auxiliary structure that speeds selected reads at the cost of storage and write maintenance. Key rules: Indexes speed reads. They slow writes. They consume space.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain B-tree Index in a production query.
interview.answer: A B-tree supports equality, ordering and range predicates and is the default PostgreSQL index type. Key rules: Default type. Supports ranges. Supports ORDER BY.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain CREATE INDEX in a production query.
interview.answer: CREATE INDEX name ON table (columns) builds an index for the chosen key. Key rules: Name indexes clearly. Choose columns from real predicates. Build concurrently on live tables.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Unique Index in a production query.
interview.answer: A unique index enforces uniqueness and also speeds equality lookups. Key rules: It enforces a rule. NULLs are allowed by default. It can back a primary key.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Composite Index in a production query.
interview.answer: A composite index keys on several columns and supports predicates that use a left-hand prefix of that key. Key rules: Order columns deliberately. The leftmost column matters most. It can cover multiple filters.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Index Column Order in a production query.
interview.answer: The first column is the primary navigation key; putting a low-selectivity column first weakens common filters on later columns. Key rules: Put equality columns first. Put range columns later. Match the query predicate.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Covering Index in a production query.
interview.answer: INCLUDE adds payload columns to a B-tree so a query can be answered from the index without visiting the heap. Key rules: INCLUDE is not a key. It increases index size. It can enable index-only scans.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Partial Index in a production query.
interview.answer: A partial index has a WHERE predicate, so it is smaller and cheaper when only a subset is queried. Key rules: Add a WHERE clause. The query predicate must imply it. It is ideal for rare statuses.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Expression Index in a production query.
interview.answer: An expression index stores a computed key such as LOWER(name), matching queries that use the same expression. Key rules: Match the expression exactly. Use it for case-insensitive lookup. It costs write time.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Hash Index in a production query.
interview.answer: A hash index supports equality comparisons only and is rarely preferable to B-tree in PostgreSQL. Key rules: Equality only. No ordering. Usually choose B-tree.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain GIN Index in a production query.
interview.answer: GIN indexes inverted lists and is used for arrays, JSONB and full-text search. Key rules: Good for containment. Large and slower to update. Use the matching operator class.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain GiST Index in a production query.
interview.answer: GiST supports extensible tree searches for geometric, range and nearest-neighbor queries. Key rules: Good for ranges and geometry. Supports exclusion constraints. Choose an operator class.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Index Selectivity in a production query.
interview.answer: Selectivity measures how many rows a predicate removes; an index helps most when the query returns a small fraction of the table. Key rules: Unique keys are highly selective. Low-selectivity filters may prefer scans. Statistics drive the choice.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain EXPLAIN in a production query.
interview.answer: EXPLAIN shows the planner’s chosen access paths, join order and estimated costs without executing the statement. Key rules: It does not run the query. Estimates come from statistics. Look for scans and sorts.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain EXPLAIN ANALYZE in a production query.
interview.answer: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and reports actual rows, loops and timing alongside estimates. Key rules: It runs the query. Use it on safe statements. Compare estimated and actual rows.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Seq Scan vs Index Scan in a production query.
interview.answer: A sequential scan reads the heap linearly, while an index scan follows the index and fetches matching heap rows. Key rules: Seq scan is fine for large fractions. Index scan wins for selective filters. Random I/O matters.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Bitmap Scan in a production query.
interview.answer: A bitmap heap scan builds a bitmap from one or more indexes and visits heap pages in physical order. Key rules: Good for medium selectivity. Combines multiple indexes. It loses exact ordering.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Index Maintenance in a production query.
interview.answer: Updates create index bloat; REINDEX rebuilds an index, and VACUUM helps the planner and heap health. Key rules: Monitor bloat. REINDEX can lock. VACUUM regularly.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Common Index Mistakes in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are indexing low-selectivity columns, duplicating an existing prefix, and expecting an index to help every query. Key rules: Check actual queries. Avoid duplicate indexes. Verify with EXPLAIN.

interview.q: Module 18 · Explain Practical Tuning in a production query.
interview.answer: Tuning starts from a slow query and its plan, adds the smallest useful index, and re-measures rather than guessing. Key rules: Capture the query. Read the plan. Add one index. Measure again.

logic.q: Module 18 · Why does GiST Index matter?
logic.answer: GiST supports extensible tree searches for geometric, range and nearest-neighbor queries. Good for ranges and geometry. Supports exclusion constraints. Choose an operator class.

logic.q: Module 18 · Why does Index Selectivity matter?
logic.answer: Selectivity measures how many rows a predicate removes; an index helps most when the query returns a small fraction of the table. Unique keys are highly selective. Low-selectivity filters may prefer scans. Statistics drive the choice.
EXPLAIN shows the planner’s chosen access paths, join order and estimated costs without executing the statement. It does not run the query. Estimates come from statistics. Look for scans and sorts.

logic.q: Module 18 · Why does EXPLAIN ANALYZE matter?
logic.answer: EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and reports actual rows, loops and timing alongside estimates. It runs the query. Use it on safe statements. Compare estimated and actual rows.

debug.title: Function mismatch
debug.broken:
CREATE INDEX idx_name ON students (LOWER(name));
SELECT * FROM students WHERE name = 'aarav';
debug.fix: SELECT * FROM students WHERE LOWER(name) = LOWER('aarav');
debug.error: The plain name predicate cannot use the expression index

debug.title: Wrong composite prefix
debug.broken:
CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_course_student ON enrollments (course_id, student_id);
SELECT * FROM enrollments WHERE student_id = 1;
debug.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_enrollments_student_course ON enrollments (student_id, course_id);
debug.error: The query does not use the leftmost column

debug.title: Duplicate index
debug.broken:
CREATE INDEX idx_students_marks ON students (marks);
CREATE INDEX idx_students_marks_again ON students (marks);
debug.error: Two indexes with the same key waste writes and space

debug.title: Unique index duplicates
debug.broken: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_students_email ON students (email);
debug.fix:
DELETE FROM students a USING students b WHERE a.id > b.id AND a.email = b.email;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_students_email ON students (email);

debug.title: Concurrent in transaction
debug.fix: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_students_marks ON students (marks);
debug.error: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block

debug.title: Partial predicate mismatch
debug.broken:
CREATE INDEX idx_known ON students (marks) WHERE marks IS NOT NULL;
SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90 OR marks IS NULL;
debug.error: The OR predicate does not imply the partial index condition

debug.title: EXPLAIN without analyze
debug.broken: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
debug.fix: EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;

debug.title: Stale statistics
debug.broken: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
debug.fix:
ANALYZE students;
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90;
debug.error: The planner may choose a plan from stale estimates

debug.title: Too many indexes
debug.fix: Keep only indexes justified by real queries and verify with pg_stat_user_indexes.
debug.error: Every write maintains all three indexes

debug.title: Nullable unique confusion
debug.broken: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_students_email ON students (email);
debug.fix: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_students_email ON students (email) WHERE email IS NOT NULL;
debug.error: Multiple NULL emails are still allowed
